newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA TO CUT, THEN SCRAP AIR TICKET TAXES.
newsitem.headline: CANADA TO CUT, THEN SCRAP AIR TICKET TAXES.

text.p: Canada will reduce and eventually eliminate its tax on air transportation as part of its program to commercialize air navigation services in Canada, Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday.

Right now, anyone buying a plane ticket for domestic or Canada-United States travel must pay a tax of up to C$55 per ticket. A C$55 tax also applies to to international travel tickets bought in Canada.
Starting January 1, 1998, people buying tickets for travel after March 1 will be taxed a maximum of C$30 per ticket, Martin said in a statement.
Once the commercialization of the air navigation system is completed, the tax will no longer apply, Martin said. The system is expected to be completed by October 31, 1998.
